newsitem.title: USA: Group says U.S. military flights hurt antelope.
newsitem.headline: Group says U.S. military flights hurt antelope.

text.p: Wildlife advocates on Friday threatened to file a lawsuit against the U.S. Marine Corps charging that training flights in the Sonoran Desert in Arizona were harming the endangered pronghorn antelope.
"This intensive onslaught of military training in the pronghorn antelope's last remaining habitat is pushing the species toward extinction," said Defenders of Wildlife president Rodger Schlickeisen.

In a letter giving the Corps 60 days notice of the upcoming lawsuit, lawyers for Defenders of Wildlife said the Marine Corps was violating the Endangered Species Act by harassing the animal and called for the Fish and Wildlife Service to review the helicopter and jet activities.
The Marine Corps had no immediate comment on the complaint. A similar case is pending against the Air Force.
